services.name: Breastfeeding Support - La Leche League New Zealand
services.description:
Questions or worries about breastfeeding? Our accredited La Leche League Leaders are experienced mothers who have been trained to provide information and support for breastfeeding. We can help over the phone, you can come along to our informal meetings, or ask a questions via email and on social media.  All of this is free and confidential.

Our mission is to help mothers to breastfeed through mother-to-mother support, education, information, and encouragement and to promote a better understanding of breastfeeding as an important element in the healthy development of the baby and mother.

La Leche League Leaders are accredited by LLLI to provide information and support for breastfeeding families. Every Leader has at least one year of breastfeeding experience as well as training in breastfeeding management and communication skills. We can help over the phone, you can come along to our informal meetings, or ask a questions via email and on social media.  All of this is free and confidential.

La Leche League has groups across the country. Groups hold regular informal discussion meetings for mothers and their babies, older children and support people are also welcome. Meetings are based on the importance of mother to mother support and cover a wide range of breastfeeding related topics. Please bring your questions, concerns and also your achievements and triumphs!

Discover the basics of breastfeeding and much more at our free monthly meetings.

La Leche League welcomes mothers, pregnant women, their children and support people to our meetings for encouragement, support, information and discussion on a wide range of breastfeeding and parenting topics. The discussion topics for the meetings are flexible depending on the needs of those present. Topics for discussion may include:

-Breastfeeding is normal
-Early days of breastfeeding
-Weaning & introduction of complementary foods
-Overcoming difficulties

Many groups also hold coffee mornings, where we meet informally in a local public space. This allows mums to come with babies, toddlers and older children, to meet other breastfeeding mums in a baby/breastfeeding/child-friendly environment.

We offer breastfeeding support and information through:

    * Lending library with books on breastfeeding, childbirth, parenting and nutrition
    * Mother-to-mother support
    * Latest breastfeeding information
    * Telephone help from experienced Leaders
    * Aroha, a bi-monthly journal for breastfeeding parents

services.serviceName: Living Violence Free - Te Noho Riri Kore
services.title: Living Violence Free - Te Noho Riri Kore
services.description:
Various Programmes and Education on Family Violence is available.

- We provide a 15 week "Support and Learning" programme which focuses on educating participants about family violence and helping them to make choices to increase the safety for themselves and their children.  

- A 16 week "Taking Responsibility to Change" programme for women who recognise their own anger is hurting those they love.  This programme is designed to help participants recognise the roots of their anger and find new ways of expressing their needs to keep themselves and their children safe.

- A 16 week "Men Living Without Violence" programme where men work in groups to  learn to stop using abusive behaviours and find new positive ways of expressing their anger.

- A 10 week "Tamariki/Children's" programme. This is an empowering & educational programme to assist children work through the impacts of being a witness or survivor of family violence. We provide individual, siblings & group sessions for children aged 5 - 14.

services.title: Taeaomanino Trust
services.description:
Taeaomanino Trust offers the following services free to families and individuals within the Wellington region.  Referrals can be received from others health and social services organisations and there is the ability for people to self-refer.  An assessment is undertaken for all new referrals.  Contact us if you would like to know more about the services and programmes we offer.

Alcohol and other Drugs Services (AOD)
We provide Client Centred individualised and group counselling programmes to assist people overcome and prevent problems with the use/misuse of alcohol and other drugs.

Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services (CAMHS)
We provide support to families, whanau and carers in maximising the individual developmental potential and mental health of infants, children, adolescent and youth between the ages of 0 – 19 years up to their twentieth birthday.

Family and Individual Counselling 
To assist Family and Individual to develop skills to cope with different life situations, to reflect and promote self-healing.

Family Violence Prevention Services
Sessions are focussed at family violence intervention to increase understanding of and to reduce the incidence of family violence.  We are piloting Family violence prevention boys/girls programmes at local Primary/Intermediate and Secondary schools.

Problem Gambling
We provide a free counselling service for people and their families experiencing any gambling related harm issues.

Whanau Ora Social Services
To providing health and social services to build the capacity of all New Zealand families in need.  It empowers whānau as a whole rather than focusing separately on individual family members and their problems.

Family Start Social Services
Child centred, family focused and free home based early intervention and preventative service for families facing challenges in the area of health, welfare and education

Social Worker in Schools
We promote and support academic and social success by supporting children, parents and teachers. We provide this both at school and in the home. We provide programmes that help children be all that they want to be.

Homebased
We provide families with assistance to make their home safe and healthy for their children and old people.

services.name: Te Waka Whaiora Trust
services.description: The Home Based Service is for a client that requires support with their house hold needs and personal care needs.  A client will be assigned to a Home Base Worker who will work with the client to enable them to manage better their household needs and personal needs.  The service is aimed at empowering the client to look after themselves within their own home environment.  The Home Base Worker will support the client to achieve key tasks such as meal planning and preparation, shopping, cleaning, washing; and medication management, personal cares such as hygiene and dressing.

services.title: Navigation Services
services.description:
The Navigation Service is a team of Navigators that are available to motivate and empower people to achieve their dreams and aspirations. 

A Navigator will work with the client and their Whanau to assist the client to access the services and supports to achieve their dreams and aspirations. A key aspect of the service is the development and implementation of a personalized plan.  The plan belongs to the client with the goals identified in order to achieve their aspirations.  The Navigator will work with the client to identify and access the appropriate services to assist in achieving the client’s goals pertaining to the plan.

services.title: Te Korowai Aroha Whānau Services
services.description:
Manaakitangata is the kaupapa/purpose underpinning Te Korowai Aroha Whānau Services. Manaakitangata means we support people with aroha, our collective pūkenga/skills and experiences we have. Our services include ‘mahi–ā–kaupapa/social support’ that includes
cultural supervision, tuākana/tēina mediation and advocacy, goal setting/planning, grief and loss, kaupapa sexual violence whānau support. We also provide ‘kōrero–ā–kaupapa’ that includes kaupapa-based therapy for individuals, couples (with tamariki), whānau and roopū/group community organisations. Lastly, Te Korowai Aroha do ‘mahere–ā–kaupapa’, which are group programmes, where we have supported whānau with mahi toi, drawing therapy, family harm programmes, youth programmes and a-wairua-based programmes.

Our  family/whanau workers are based in Wellington, Hutt Valley, Porirua and Kapiti and are mobile. They can work with people in their own homes, our office or community settings.  We can work with families, individuals and groups we also offer educational programmes and support groups, including programmes for children. The work we do involves providing information on mental health and addiction, the services and treatments available and practical support to access health and community services. We also can provide information and support on the things that family can do to respond, help and keep themselves well when the family is affected by mental illness and addiction. 
As well as the support our Family/whanau offers we can provide free counselling using volunteer counsellors.

services.name: SPELD NZ Inc - Mana Local Liaison Group
services.description:
SPELD NZ, established in the 1970s, is a nationwide, not-for-profit organisation registered with the Charities Commission (CC46602).  SPELD NZ works with people with dyslexia and other specific learning disabilities (SLD).  SPELD NZ provides:
•	comprehensive diagnostic assessment for dyslexia and other SLD by qualified assessors with SPELD NZ training
•	one-on-one tuition, for adults and children, by qualified teachers with SPELD NZ training
•	support for families and whanau (eg. webinars, library, magazine, Facebook and YouTube)
•	training for parents, whanau, teachers, teacher aides, assessors and other interested professionals

SPELD NZ has three regional offices which co-ordinate services throughout New Zealand. The SPELD NZ National Office is based in Auckland.

See also:
A two-day Introduction to Specific Learning Disabilities course is available to all those interested.  SPELD NZ also trains SPELD NZ Teachers and Assessors.  For more information, please see the Training page of www.speld.org.nz or call 0800 773 536.

services.title: Te Whare Tiaki Wahine Refuge
services.description:
Women's Refuges provide help with:
- Support to obtain Court Orders e.g Protection, Parenting etc
- Support if required at Domestic Violence related court appearances
- Support to apply for Legal Aid
- Support to contact Lawyers for appointments
- Support Wahiine who are dealing with the Police, Oranga Tamariki - Ministry for Children, MSD-Work and Income, Kāinga Ora-Housing
- Support to contact or follow up with MSD/Kāinga Ora to find Safe long term Accommodation
- Finding Local Domestic Violence Education pPogrammes and Counselling.

In addition, they offer:
- 24 hour Phone Crisis Line
- Refuge Safe House Short-Term Accommodation. 
- Domestic Violence Training and Policy advice 
- Services targeted to meet the needs of the Maori, Pacific Island, Asian or Migrant, general populations of New Zealand. 

In an Emergency, if you and your whanau are in Danger - Please phone 111

services.name: Victim Support - Porirua
services.description:
- Emotional support: We’re someone independent you can talk to. We listen without judgement, and support you to identify ways to cope.

- Practical assistance: We’ll work with you to develop a support plan, access financial assistance if you’re eligible, link you with community resources, and advocate on your behalf.

- Information: We’ll help you understand your rights, what happens next, how to access resources and support you to make informed choices.

- Criminal justice/coronial process support: We’ll help you feel informed, prepared and supported through the justice system, including court attendance costs, if eligible.

- Referrals: You may find our help is enough. However, we’ll help you connect with other support services and counselling, when appropriate.

Family Works is a family-focused social service agency supporting children, young people, families and communities to thrive and reach their full potential. We can help you and your whānau through challenging and confusing times to make positive lasting change.

Services include:
- social work and advocacy
- counselling and therapy
- family violence prevention and safety
- mediation and dispute resolution
- youth mentoring
- parenting education and support
- service coordination.

services.title: Playcentre (Early Childhood Education)
services.description:
Playcentre offers a unique approach to early childhood education based on the belief that learning is a shared journey between tamariki and their whānau. Parents and caregivers are recognised as a child’s first and most important teachers, which is why they attend alongside their children, actively participating in play, learning, and development.

For families with children aged 0–6, Playcentre provides a welcoming, community-focused environment where whānau can connect, build friendships, and support one another. It is especially valuable for those new to parenting or new to a community, creating a strong sense of belonging in a friendly and inclusive space.

Learning at Playcentre is child-led and play-based. Tamariki are encouraged to explore their interests and develop at their own pace in environments set up to cater for different ages, stages, and abilities. This approach nurtures creativity, confidence, imagination, and social connection. Learning is guided by Te Whāriki, New Zealand’s bicultural early childhood curriculum, supporting holistic development grounded in Aotearoa’s unique cultural context.

Playcentre also supports parent education. Enrolled whānau can access a free NZQA-accredited adult education programme, building skills, confidence, and understanding of child development. This strengthens both parenting capability and children’s learning experiences.

As a registered charity with around 400 centres nationwide, Playcentre is an affordable and accessible early learning option. Families can visit up to three times before enrolling, offering a chance to experience the supportive and engaging environment firsthand.

Overall, Playcentre combines quality early education with strong whānau involvement and community connection.

To find your local centre visit www.playcentre.org.nz

services.name: Strengthening Families - Porirua
services.description:
Coordinated support and facilitation process for families/whanau with at least one child under 17 within the family (can include grandparents raising grandchildren, or families with children returning home out of care etc), who are working with two or more government, community agencies, Churches, Marae etc. 
Whaanau Wananga is for families who want to make positive change to their lives and already have some agencies involved, but things aren't working as they would like. WW coordinators bring together family, whanau and agencies to work out a plan the family want. There may be several issues around school, home, health, children, disabilities, justice etc that the family want to change and improve. They direct the process and choose who needs to be at meetings, where everyone can sit round the table together to work out a plan. It is a coordinated approach with an independent facilitator to run meetings where families choose who attends and what they want the outcomes to be. After the initial meeting the family decide if they need further meetings and in what timeframe. The average is 2-3 meetings per family, but families with complex situations have as many meetings as they decide they need to reach the best, most sustainable outcomes.

services.description:
WELLfed nourishes & connects communities. 

WELLfed delivers FREE adult education programme based around food & cooking skills. WELLfed is interactive classes, held weekly.  WELLfed adult Learners practise come together to learn skills & make kai together.  We practise how to:
- plan, shop, safely prepare and cook low-cost healthy meals 
- best use fresh fruit and vegetables 
- budget & find ingredients to get more for our dollar
- safe food handling and storage

WELLfed can also connect our Learners with other free courses including driver license education, first aid courses, CV writing and more. 

WELLfed has been co-designed with the local community, to make the classes accessible and to ensure that the recipes and classes make a real difference.
 
Our programme delivers a series of interactive cooking classes, held weekly in the communities that need it most.

services.name: Porirua Elim Church Trust
services.description:
EKHO is a Oscar service in Porirua, that provides after school care and holiday programme for children aged 5-12yrs old. We believe in the importance and value of children, that they are significant and competent learners. The greatest gift we can give a child is the confidence to develop self-esteem through activities that reinforce individual worth and value.

We offer a variety of activities in both our after school and holiday programmes, giving children opportunities to learn sewing, dance, cooking, baking, creative arts, Bible lessons, and many other fun experiences. We also encourage the celebration and learning of Pacific Island language weeks to help children connect with diverse cultures.

Our holiday programme includes plenty of outdoor activities, along with excursions to local pools, playgrounds, movies, and more.

If you are looking for a programme that helps shapes, builds and supports your child’s learning and potential, then you have come to the right place! We are proud to offer out-of-school programmes to suit you the parent but most importantly your children.

services.description: SWIS provide programs, one on one or group support to tamariki who are having difficulty in school due to a number of reasons. SWIS work collaboratively with the schools, whanau and tamariki to develop plans to better enhance education stability.

services.title: Whanau Resilience
services.description:
Whanau resilience is a long term support service that aims to create strong, resilient communities where whanau are supported to live violence free and to eliminate violence for the next generation.

Whanau resilience strengthen cultural identity and whakapapa, enhance social capability and community connection to develop long term outcomes/goals for tane and wahine usig violence, support whanau to address trauma healing and recovery from violence, and learn to create healthy relationships.

services.title: Youth Mentor

services.name: Porirua Community Corrections
services.description:
If you are serving a community sentence or you have been released from prison on parole or with special conditions, you are “on probation”.

Our Probation Officers work with people on probation to motivate them to make changes in their lives. This may include attending Community Work or programmes to address violence, alcohol and drug abuse or driving offences. If appropriate, offenders can attend programmes that teach them about Maori culture and give them opportunity to re-connect to their iwi.

To find out more about the services of Corrections, reporting to a Community Corrections site, community sentences and programmes, partnering with Corrections or for help with your local community project, contact your local site or visit https://www.corrections.govt.nz/.
